findings.text: follow-on: materialize_machine_artifact passes rename_factory=_linux_rename_no_replace explicitly, so it bypasses the new _publication_rename_factory probe and still raises the unsupported-no-clobber error on GPFS; the probe's reach is one in-tree caller short, leaving machine-artifact publication unsupported on the shared filesystems.

follow-on: the base-arm header's module= line names the worktree's content_store.py while its tree= line names the scratch base tree, so the header alone does not identify the revision exercised; the traceback line content_store.py:542 (base numbering, against 590 in the head module) is what proves the base source ran.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against b70052ffb; 382cee25b carries the whole code and test change (content_store.py +105, tests +227), and 93b1c2a49/7291442af/7d990dd57/27ce7001b touch only the evidence fragment, so the after_suite revision 93b1c2a49 is the reviewed code.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names tests/test_content_store.py plus an H200 end-to-end row set; tests/test_content_store.py is recorded green (after_suite 10 passed, EXIT=0) against a 4-failure base arm, and h200-cs-1287385.out records the 282/550/2098-cell value and jet rows exit 0 with bitwise-equal loaded matrices.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is for the default operand cache to publish on GPFS through content_store's rename hook; nova/database/content_store.py:396-649 adds a capability probe and a plain-renameat fallback selected behind the existing rename_factory hook, and scripts/prototypes/read_route/jets.py:143 (publish_operand -> publish_files, no factory) publishes through it unchanged.
item_verdicts.manifest: read in full; it records status complete, five commits, the negative-control log path and note (9 failed, 1 passed with the crash check among the failures), baseline_suite 4 failed/6 passed, after_suite 0 failed/10 passed, measurement_module and measurement_cwd, and the H200 job 1287385 figures.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares nova/database/content_store.py, tests/test_content_store.py and docs/evidence/fragments/converged-forward-solve/content-store-gpfs.html; git diff --stat b70052ffb..27ce7001b touches exactly those three paths and nothing else.

justifications.durability: reverting the marker check at nova/database/content_store.py:282-285 reddens tests/test_content_store.py:test_entry_without_completion_marker_is_not_served, and the base arm reddens the four GPFS publication checks, so the added guards fail on the regressions they cover.
justifications.evidence: the after suite and the H200 job are recorded with exit status and per-row figures, but baseline-content-store.log:2 names the worktree module in its module= line rather than the base scratch tree its tree= line names, so the header alone does not fix the revision the base arm measured.
justifications.fit: the added helpers (_linux_rename_replace, _rename_no_replace_supported, _publication_rename_factory) follow the private-helper idiom of nova/database/content_store.py:369 and carry no plan or ticket label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: nova/database/content_store.py:644-649 selects plain renameat on a GPFS root and scripts/prototypes/read_route/jets.py:143 publishes through it unedited, so the default operand cache publishes on GPFS; nova/imas/machine_artifact.py:758 still pins the no-clobber primitive and is the one in-tree caller the probe does not reach.
justifications.reuse: a search over nova for renameat/RENAME_NOREPLACE/os.replace found the rename owners only in nova/database/content_store.py:369-434 and the single-file atomic checkpoint at nova/equilibrium/fixed_point.py:190-216, a different capability, so the additions extend the owner rather than fork it.
